inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 28 Feb 2026: 2,263.7m shares in issue (FY2026 AR p.? 'Number of shares in issue 2,263,689,189', line 11344) + 46.6m weighted dilutive share options (note 'Weighted average number of dilutive share options', line 8946). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so the ongoing GBP200m core buyback is the cash that keeps the count flat and is value-neutral here. The FY2027 GBP300m programme (GBP200m core + GBP100m bank-proceeds return) will have reduced the count by roughly 50-60m by October 2026, but the balance sheet is also 28 Feb 2026, so count and net debt are kept on the same vintage rather than mixing a newer count with an older cash balance.
inputs.net_debt_note: net_debt is the company's Retail net debt EXCLUDING lease liabilities, GBP203m at 28 Feb 2026 (FY2026 AR financial review line 2333; note 31). It is not total_debt - cash because the group cash of GBP1,067m includes GBP334m deposited at central banks by the residual Financial Services entity (note 30), which the retail net-debt definition excludes, and because hedging derivatives are included. Lease liabilities (GBP5,540m) are deliberately excluded from net debt -- see lease_treatment.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR note A2.1 / note 6: share-based payments expense GBP75m group (GBP72m retail) cash-flow add-back; no separate equity-award tax line disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes KPI = 0), so the add-back is the combined figure
inputs.buyback_note: GBP251m purchase of own shares for cancellation in FY2026 (financing activities, A2.1 line 11134), plus GBP64m own shares bought for employee schemes. FY2027 guided GBP300m (GBP200m core + GBP100m return of bank disposal proceeds). Repurchaser: the flat count is funded.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP/share to quoted pence. No dual listing to parity-check; the magnitude check is that per-share values in pounds (~GBP3) land in the hundreds of pence once converted, the same order as the quote.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: 28 February / early March (52-week year; FY2026 = 52 weeks to 28 Feb 2026)
inputs.balance_sheet_vintage_note: The FY2026 annual report (balance sheet 28 Feb 2026) is the latest filing with a balance sheet; the Q1 FY2027 trading statement (30 Jun 2026) carries sales only. The H1 FY2027 interim (~Nov 2026) will refresh net debt and the share count after ~7 months of the GBP300m buyback.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP: 10y gilt ~4.6%, UK ERP 5.0%, equity beta ~0.70 for a defensive UK grocer -> cost of equity ~8.1%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.5% (Jan-2025 sterling bond issuance), ~4.1% after tax; ex-lease net debt (GBP203m) is ~3% of enterprise value, so WACC rounds to 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios -- competitive and margin risk is priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate (adaptations (f)).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Sainsbury's carries GBP5,540m of IFRS-16 lease liabilities against GBP1,061m of borrowings, so the lease choice is the single biggest lever in this model. The full lease cash cost -- GBP504m capital repayment (financing, A2.1 line 11136) + GBP266m lease interest (net finance costs on lease liabilities, line 2220) = GBP770m, 2.29% of revenue -- is charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt (net_debt = GBP203m retail non-lease). D&A for the cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: FY2026 underlying D&A GBP1,186m less ~GBP530m ROU depreciation (note 6) = ~GBP656-700m, ~2.0% of revenue, matching FY2027 guidance of ~GBP1.2bn D&A 'including GBP0.5bn right-of-use asset depreciation'. This mirrors the company's own Retail free cash flow definition (after lease principal and interest), which is the clean FY2026 anchor (GBP574m) and the FY2027 guidance (>GBP500m). Charging both lease cash and lease liabilities would be the double-count the adaptations file warns of.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US', owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md read in full: currency (GBP flows, GBp quote), material leases (treatment B), SBC-light market). Not a bank/REIT: Sainsbury's Bank was sold to NatWest (completed FY2026) and Argos Financial Services to NewDay (Jul 2025); the residual Financial Services segment is in run-off and is excluded from the flows, its cash from net debt, and its remaining GBP100m of proceeds is being returned via the FY2027 buyback. FCF BASE: the CSV FY2026 reported FCF of GBP931m (OCF 1,774 - capex 843) is NOT the anchor -- group OCF includes bank wind-down flows (+GBP1.8bn financial assets released, -GBP2.0bn customer deposits leaving, GBP400m intragroup bank dividend). last_fcf (931-75-24 = 832) is recorded for contract consistency only. The forward build is anchored to the RETAIL cash-flow statement (A2.1): underlying EBITDA GBP2,211m (6.57% of revenue), lease cash GBP770m, capex GBP843m (FY2024's GBP1,559m included a one-off property-portfolio purchase and is not run-rate), cash tax GBP112m, retail FCF GBP574m. Normalised unlevered owner FCF from that statement is ~GBP450m at the actual cash-tax rate (574 + 64 non-lease interest - 23 interest income - 128 working-capital inflow + 80 non-underlying costs - 41 disposal proceeds - 75 SBC) and ~GBP370m at a normalised 27% cash tax; the component build's year-1 owner FCF of ~GBP435m sits between the two. INTEREST INCOME: not stripped from the forward flows (the engine builds from EBITDA, which excludes it) and not material -- net debt, not net cash. DIVIDENDS: FY2026 GBP566m includes a GBP250m special from bank proceeds; the ordinary run-rate is ~GBP316m. ANALYSIS JSON: arrived after the first build; its bull/bear axes (discounter and Tesco price pressure, Argos ASP decline, Nectar360 retail media >=GBP100m incremental profit target to Mar 2027, GBP1bn cost programme, lease leverage, FY2027 guidance disappointing at the April 2026 results, Middle East cost/demand uncertainty) were checked against the scenario narratives and moved no driver.

historical_growth.retail_fcf_note: Owner-FCF CAGRs are computed on reported FCF - SBC - interest income (FY2021 1,716 / FY2023 1,370 / FY2026 832) and are meaningless: the group cash-flow statement carried Sainsbury's Bank deposit and financial-asset swings of GBP1-2bn a year until the FY2026 disposal. The company's Retail free cash flow (post lease principal and interest) is the usable series: FY2025 GBP531m, FY2026 GBP574m, FY2027 guided >GBP500m.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative (-5.4% 3yr, -1.4% 5yr) because distributions, buybacks and the bank disposal shrank book value faster than retained earnings; EPS CAGR (24% 3yr) is a recovery from the FY2023 trough. Neither is a growth proxy for a 2%-a-year grocer; revenue CAGR used, cross-checked against Q1 FY2027 retail sales +2.7% (LFL +2.1%, net space +0.5%).
historical_growth.notes: FY2026 EPS 16.9p vs 8.8p FY2023; book value GBP6,150m vs GBP7,253m.

base.growth_rationale: Q1 FY2027 retail sales +2.7% (LFL +2.1%, net space +0.5% from ~10 supermarkets and ~20 convenience openings); UK food inflation 2-3%; fuel volumes drifting down. 2.5% fading to 2.0% nominal.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY2027 guidance: underlying operating profit GBP975-1,075m + D&A ~GBP1.2bn = ~GBP2,225m on ~GBP34.5bn revenue = 6.45% (FY2026 6.57%, FY2025 6.68% -- the decline is higher depreciation from the space programme). Modest recovery to 6.6% as Argos restructuring and the GBP1bn cost-saving programme offset price investment.
base.lease_rationale: FY2026 lease cash GBP770m = 2.29% of revenue; held at 2.3% as new supermarkets add leases roughly in line with sales.
base.da_rationale: Ex-ROU underlying D&A ~GBP0.7bn (FY2027 guidance GBP1.2bn incl. GBP0.5bn ROU) = 2.0%.
base.capex_rationale: FY2027 guidance GBP800-850m core retail capex = 2.4% of revenue; FY2026 2.5%; FY2024's 4.8% was the one-off property-portfolio purchase.
base.tax_rationale: FY2026 cash tax GBP112m was ~16% of modelled EBIT (full-expensing capital allowances, timing of SBC deductions); P&L underlying rate guided ~29% (above the 25% statutory rate because UK gives no allowances on most building spend). Cash rate ramped 20% -> 27% over five years, below the P&L rate because capex-driven allowances persist while capex continues.
base.wc_rationale: Grocer negative working capital: payables exceed inventory + receivables, so growth releases cash. FY2026's GBP128m inflow (15% of the revenue increase) was flattered by payment-term improvements; 5% capture of the revenue change is the run-rate.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 8%/2% is 17x FCF; capped at 16x -- a mature grocer growing with nominal GDP does not command a 20x exit.

scenario_narratives.base: Sainsbury's keeps its share-gaining momentum in food (Q1 FY2027 grocery +3.6%, volume growth, Aldi Price Match and Nectar Prices holding value perception) while general merchandise and Argos shrink deliberately in favour of food space. Revenue grows 2.5% fading to 2%, underlying EBITDA margin holds 6.45-6.6% as the GBP1bn cost programme, Nectar360 retail media and Argos restructuring offset continued price investment and rising depreciation from ~10 new supermarkets a year. Retail FCF runs GBP500-600m a year as guided; the GBP200m core buyback and ~GBP320m ordinary dividend are funded from it. Lease cash stays ~2.3% of sales; cash tax drifts up toward 27% as capital allowances normalise.
scenario_narratives.bull: Asda's price-led reset under Allan Leighton fails to regain share, Sainsbury's continues to take trolley-shop share from both Asda and Morrisons, fresh food and Taste the Difference premiumisation lift mix, Nectar360 retail media scales as a high-margin income line and Argos's turnaround reaches a sustainable ~GBP100m profit. Revenue grows 3.5% fading to 2.5%; underlying EBITDA margin expands 50bp to 7.0% by year 6; capex eases to 2.3% once the space programme matures; working capital captures 7% of growth. Exit multiple 18x, terminal growth 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: A sustained UK grocery price war -- Asda's reset, Aldi and Lidl space growth, Tesco matching -- forces Sainsbury's to reinvest the cost savings and more; margin erodes 60bp to 6.0% and stays there; volume gains fade and revenue grows only 1-1.5% nominal while fuel and general merchandise decline. Capex stays at 2.5% to defend the estate and lease costs edge up to 2.35% as sales densities fall. Employer NIC and wage inflation outrun pricing. Terminal growth 1.5%, exit 14x. No solvency question: ex-lease net debt is GBP203m and fixed-charge cover ~3x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35. Bear raised from 15% because a 60bp margin move is nearly 10% of EBITDA for a 6.5%-margin grocer and the UK market has three price-aggressive competitors (Asda reset, Aldi, Lidl) -- the downside is margin, not solvency, but it is the more likely tail. Bull cut from 35% because margin expansion to 7% needs several independent things to go right (Asda's reset failing, Argos turning, retail media scaling, cost saves not reinvested) in a market where excess returns are competed away.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A mature, 6.5%-EBITDA-margin UK grocer valued on unlevered owner FCF after the full lease cash cost, with lease liabilities excluded from net debt so the GBP5.5bn of IFRS-16 leases is charged exactly once. The forward build is anchored to the company's own Retail free cash flow (FY2026 GBP574m, FY2027 >GBP500m guided) rather than the bank-distorted group cash-flow statement. Value is dominated by the terminal year (capped at 16x FCF in the base case), so the answer is mostly a view on sustainable margin and on what a 2%-growth grocer is worth at exit.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin: every 10bp of EBITDA margin is ~GBP35m of EBITDA, ~GBP25m of after-tax FCF and roughly 15-17p/share at a 16x exit -- the bear case's 60bp erosion is the dominant downside

Lease treatment: switching to treatment (A) (leases in net debt, lease cash added back) must be done wholesale -- deducting GBP5.5bn of lease liabilities while also charging GBP770m/yr of lease cash would halve the value and is wrong
Terminal multiple: Gordon at 8%/2% is 17x; the 16x cap binds in the base case, so terminal_cap_multiple is a judgement, not a derived number
Cash tax: the ramp from ~16% actual to 27% removes ~GBP80m/yr of FCF by year 6; if full-expensing allowances persist indefinitely the base is conservative by ~25p/share
Balance-sheet vintage: net debt and share count are 28 Feb 2026; ~GBP175m of buyback has run since, which is value-neutral in this model but will move the per-share figure at the H1 FY2027 refresh
Analysis JSON arrived after the first build and was reconciled; its bear point that FY2027 guidance already disappointed in April 2026 is consistent with the 6.45% year-1 EBITDA margin
